html:
US relations with Ukraine have severely deteriorated today following Trump’s decision to waive several Russia sanctions, which he claims are against US national interests. This move has prompted Ukraine to resume strikes on Russian oil refineries and seek increased backing from European allies, while Defence Minister Guido Crosetto told the BBC the US risks prolonging Russia's full-scale invasion.

Russia-Ukraine Conflict: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has turned to Europe for support, asking Brussels for an additional €70 billion to fund the war, as his relationship with Trump deteriorated. Ukraine has resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries, with Russian authorities confirming a strike southeast of Moscow. EU leaders have reaffirmed support for Ukraine, though a significant budget hole poses a challenge. Russian strikes have also killed six people in Ukraine and cut power to 370,000 in the Volyn region, while reports describe daily life in Kyiv as Russia attempts to make it unlivable.

Middle East Security: Tensions in the Middle East are high as the US military weighs the use of the 'mother of all bombs' in potential future strikes against Iran. This comes as an oil supertanker reportedly struck a naval mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran’s Army chief stating the Strait will remain closed until Iran's rights are respected. Saudi Arabia has accused Houthi attacks, some with Iran's targeting and intelligence support, of violating its rapprochement terms with Iran, while the Saudi-led coalition intercepted missiles and drones. Meanwhile, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians and a Washington Post photojournalist during the olive harvest in the West Bank.

Global Economy & Social Unrest: Protests have intensified across several nations, including France, where the Yellow Vests movement against rising fuel prices is gaining momentum, and Albania, where demonstrators demand Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation over university conditions. In Argentina, education cut protests led to clashes, while thousands of Gen Z protesters in India were detained over alleged voter fraud. On the economic front, Social Security benefits are set for a boost to offset rising consumer prices, and some Australian suburbs are seeing mortgage repayments become cheaper than rent.

US Administration Turnover: The White House saw rapid turnover today as White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was "let go" from her role, just five days after her appointment. Trump had signaled her departure following media scrutiny of her legal credentials, including an admission that she had not passed the bar. Reports suggest Susie Wiles helped orchestrate the press secretary's exit through a Fox interview.

Other Global Developments: Brazil has reported a record fall in Amazon deforestation ahead of a key election, though Meta employees reportedly hindered Lula's accounts during the campaign. Pope Leo was pictured for the first time since surgery and a cancer diagnosis, celebrating Mass at the hospital. Separately, Irish author Sally Rooney's books will no longer be sold in the UK after she pledged royalties to a banned pro-Palestinian group.
